title: Degraded prefetch coordination caused cascading circuit trips and uneven shed — postmortem & action plan
text:
Degraded prefetch coordination caused cascading circuit trips and uneven shed — postmortem & action plan

description:
Incident where a coordinated change to request prefetching and autoscaler heuristics led to simultaneous fanout into backing nodes across two regions, triggering circuit-breaker trips and aggressive load-shedding that caused SLO misses for chat and generation endpoints. This doc captures timeline, root cause, mitigations, and tracked follow-ups.

impact_summary:
SLO breach for generation/chat endpoints affecting approx 6% of requests across two regions during a 2h 23m window. Customer-facing errors and elevated tail latency caused degraded UX for several high-traffic tenants. No data loss or security incident.

incident_timeline:
2026-02-26T09:12Z - Autoscaler config (release autoscale/enable-prefetch) rolled to 20% of fleet (canary).
2026-02-26T09:47Z - Prefetch change promoted to 80% after initial canary signals (manual).
2026-02-26T10:05Z - Traffic spike detected from onboarding customer X performing large batched inference jobs (token surge +70% over baseline).
2026-02-26T10:10Z - Tiered circuit-breakers begin opening in eu-west-1 due to queue length and cache warmup latency; traffic shifts to us-west-2 as primary region for some customers.
2026-02-26T10:17Z - us-west-2 sees synchronous endpoint fanout; host-level KV cache misses increase, token latency 99p crosses 1.2s. SLO alert triggers (99p latency > 750ms).
2026-02-26T10:25Z - Automated load-shedding policy activates aggressively on several priority queues; downstream services observe cascading drops and retries.
2026-02-26T11:30Z - Engineering throttles prefetch feature via runtime feature flag and increases circuit hysteresis windows. Manual capacity bump applied to both regions.
2026-02-26T11:48Z - Traffic begins to normalize; SLOs recover to baseline around 12:35Z after rolling back prefetch promotion and extra capacity stabilizes queues.

slo_metrics:
Target: 99th percentile latency < 750ms for text-generation endpoints
Observed: 99th percentile peaked at 1.24s at 2026-02-26T10:17Z
Duration: 2 hours 23 minutes (alerts window 10:10Z–12:33Z)
Error rate: increased from 0.6% to 4.8% for priority customers during peak
Affected regions: eu-west-1 (primary), us-west-2 (failover surge)

root_cause:
Two changes combined in production under load: (1) a prefetch optimization that issued speculative requests to warm KV caches and (2) an autoscaler heuristics change that allowed faster instance cycling. Under a sudden external batched token surge these led to synchronized inbound fanout across hosts, producing high backend cache miss amplification and queue growth that tripped region-level circuit breakers. Circuit hysteresis and shedding thresholds were insufficiently conservative, which caused aggressive shedding and retry storms that amplified the failure.

contributing_factors:
Prefetch rollout was promoted to 80% without extended chaos testing for multi-region failover scenarios
Autoscaler change reduced cold-start smoothing window; simultaneous scaling behavior amplified fanout
Circuit-breaker hysteresis configured per-region but lacked cross-region coordination (no backoff coupling)
Load-shedding policy was tuned to preserve tail latency but had a single global aggressiveness parameter; it mis-prioritized some priority queues
Monitoring alert thresholds were based on 99p sampled on rolling 5m windows which delayed earlier detection of gradual tail climb

mitigations_taken:
Immediate rollback of prefetch promotion to previous canary percentage
Feature-flagged prefetch to disable on affected customer groups until safe rollout
Increased circuit-breaker hysteresis (min-open window +30s) and added randomized retry jitter
Manual capacity bump (temporary reserved instances) to absorb spike
Adjusted load-shedding aggressiveness for priority queues to reduce retry amplification

postmortem_findings:
Speculative prefetching is beneficial for warm workloads but creates correlated load patterns when combined with fast autoscale churn
Circuit-breaker configs need cross-region coordination to avoid asymmetric open/close patterns
Rate-limiting for speculative prefetch should be enforced per-shard with global caps to prevent simultaneous fanout
We lacked a dedicated synthetic failover test that exercises the entire failover path under bursty token surges
Alerting windows should include a combination of short (30s) and medium (5m) tail-latency detectors with regional aggregation

action_items:
ENG-127892 - Introduce per-shard rate limiter for speculative prefetch and global cap; owner: Ethan Park; due: 2026-03-12
ENG-127893 - Update autoscaler smooth-window to prevent synchronized churn during scale-up events; owner: Liam Chen; due: 2026-03-08
ENG-127894 - Implement cross-region circuit state coupling and staggered backoff policy; owner: Marina Gomez; due: 2026-03-19
ENG-127895 - Add synthetic chaos test that simulates token-surge plus failover across two regions, run in CI nightly; owner: Sofia Ruiz; due: 2026-03-05
ENG-127896 - Revise load-shedding priorities and add protection for priority customers with adaptive thresholds; owner: Asha Patel; due: 2026-03-15
ENG-127897 - Expand alerting: add 30s tail-latency detector and regional aggregation dashboard; owner: DevOps Team (lead: Marina Gomez); due: 2026-03-10
ENG-127898 - Document runbook updates for forced-prefetch rollback and manual capacity bump procedures; owner: Marina Gomez; due: 2026-03-01

followups:
Circuit config rollout to be canaryed with explicit cross-region traffic shaping in Cycle 43
Design review scheduled for speculative prefetch: gating points, telemetry, and rate limits (2026-03-02 design RFC)
Customer outreach: targeted emails to affected tenants summarizing incident, mitigations, and compensatory credits (Customer Success owns)

runbook_changes:
Add a step to feature-flagging runbook: verify synthetic failover test pass before >30% rollout
Add explicit rollback path for prefetch and autoscaler changes with verification queries
Add playbook for manual capacity bump including CRM contact list and cost authorization steps

notes:
This incident surfaced a common systems pattern: independent optimizations (speculation + faster scaling) that are safe in isolation can interact nonlinearly under bursty external load. Our remediations focus on reducing correlated fanout, improving early detection, and increasing canary discipline.
